# dsh-request-image-cap
Clamps every image sent to the model to a pixel cap, so many-image requests stop failing.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Keep every image DSH transmits inside the provider's **per-side** pixel limit.
## Why

The Anthropic Messages API accepts 8000 px per side for an ordinary request but
only **2000 px per s
ide once the request carries many images**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both DSH image gates are **area** gates:
| stage | knob | default |
| ingest (`dsh-attachment-local`) | `normalizedImageMaxPixels` / `normalizedImageMaxDimension` | 4 1

94 304 px² / 8192 px |
| request projection (`requestImageDimensions`) | `llm-pi-ai.requestImagePixe
lBudget` | 4 194 304 px² |

A full-page screenshot therefore lands in the store as e.g. `828x5059` (inside
the area budget, far

outside the per-side rule) and is transmitted verbatim.
The failure is latent: the same image is fin

e in a short request and only kills
a long session later, then on every retry, because the bytes are

already in the
history.
## What it does

Wraps `ctx.attachments.readImageRequest(ref, policy, signal)` (the single seam
every LLM adapter use

s to materialise request bytes) and converts a per-side
cap into the area budget that produces it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`requestImageDimensions` scales by `sqrt(maxPixels/(w*h))` and floors, so the
long edge lands at or
under `cap`, aspect ratio preserved.

* **retroactive**: acts at request time, so histories that already contain
oversized images become s

ever widens** a route policy that is already tighter;
* **fails safe**: if a core upgrade renames th
anything above ~1.15 MP server-side anyway.

## Install
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-request-image-cap`, or from GitHub:
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-request-image-cap`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so it joins `dsh.profile.bundles` and its own patch
inserts the e

ntry. Override values with a `- id: request-image-cap` row (`config:` only, no
second `insert`) in y

our profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. It mounts at boot: restart `dsh web`
after installing; the log the

n shows `request-image-cap: active, 2000px per side`.
A local checkout works too: `dsh plugin --prof

ile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-request-image-cap`.
Requires Node 22.18 or newer; used on DSH
0.1.5 and 0.2.1 (the seam is `ctx.attachments.readImageRequest`).

The real fix belongs in `requestImageDimensions`: a route-owned
`maxDimension` beside `maxPixels`. T
his plugin is the local stand-in.
